# 1. Package setup

The installation code checks for missing packages; packages that are already available are skipped. It is disabled by default during report rendering to avoid modifying the environment unexpectedly. Run it once interactively if needed.

```{r}
#| label: install-packages
#| eval: false
# =====================================================
# INSTALL PACKAGES ONLY IF NOT ALREADY INSTALLED
# =====================================================

# Function to check and install CRAN packages
install_if_missing <- function(pkg, repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org") {
  if (!requireNamespace(pkg, quietly = TRUE)) {
    message("Installing: ", pkg)
    install.packages(pkg, repos = repos)
  } else {
    message("Already installed: ", pkg)
  }
}

# 1. CRAN packages
cran_packages <- c(
  "devtools",
  "DSI",
  "DSOpal",
  "opalr",
  "metafor",
  "readr",
  "knitr",
  "kableExtra"
)

for (pkg in cran_packages) {
  install_if_missing(pkg)
}

# 2. R-universe package
install_if_missing(
  "dsTidyverseClient",
  repos = c(
    "https://molgenis.r-universe.dev",
    "https://cloud.r-project.org"
  )
)

# 3. GitHub packages
install_github_if_missing <- function(pkg, repo) {
  if (!requireNamespace(pkg, quietly = TRUE)) {
    message("Installing from GitHub: ", pkg)
    
    devtools::install_github(
      repo,
      upgrade = "never",
      dependencies = NA
    )
  } else {
    message("Already installed: ", pkg)
  }
}

install_github_if_missing(
  "dsBaseClient",
  "datashield/dsBaseClient"
)

install_github_if_missing(
  "dsOMOPClient",
  "isglobal-brge/dsOMOPClient@2.7.1"
)

install_github_if_missing(
  "dsOmicsClient",
  "isglobal-brge/dsOmicsClient"
)

# 4. Verify installed packages
all_packages <- c(
  cran_packages,
  "dsTidyverseClient",
  "dsBaseClient",
  "dsOMOPClient",
  "dsOmicsClient"
)

installation_status <- data.frame(
  Package = all_packages,
  Installed = vapply(
    all_packages,
    requireNamespace,
    logical(1),
    quietly = TRUE
  )
)

print(installation_status)

```

```{r}
library(DSI)
```

# 4. Connect to remote Opal servers


## Configure Opal connections

Credentials are read from environment variables. Configure them in your local `.Renviron` file (never commit that file).

Set `DS_FRANCE_USER`, `DS_FRANCE_PASSWORD`, `DS_ISGLOBAL_USER`, and `DS_ISGLOBAL_PASSWORD` in your local environment before rendering.

```{r}
#| label: workshop-04
builder <- DSI::newDSLoginBuilder()

# Server 1: France 
builder$append(
  server = 'France', 
  url = "https://opal-demo.obiba.org",
  user = "administrator", 
  password = "password",
  table = "CNSIM.CNSIM1",
  profile = "default"
)

# Server 2: Spain (ISGlobal)
builder$append(
  server = 'ISGlobal', 
  url = "https://opal.isglobal.org/repo",
  user = "invited", 
  password = "12345678Aa@",
  table = "CNSIM.CNSIM2",
  profile = "rock-inma"
)
```


## Log in and assign remote datasets

```{r}
#| label: workshop-05
logindata <- builder$build()
conns <- datashield.login(logins = logindata, assign = TRUE, symbol = "D")
```

## Create Boolean indicators

```{r}
#| label: workshop-28
ds.Boole(
  V1 = "D$PM_BMI_CONTINUOUS",
  V2 = "25",
  Boolean.operator = ">=",
  numeric.output = TRUE,
  newobj = "BMI.25.plus")

ds.Boole(
  V1 = "D$LAB_GLUC_ADJUSTED",
  V2 = "6",
  Boolean.operator = "<",
  numeric.output = TRUE,
  newobj = "GLUC.6.less")
```

```{r}
# List remote objects
ds.ls()

# Frequency of the BMI indicator
ds.table("BMI.25.plus")

# Frequency of the glucose indicator
ds.table("GLUC.6.less")
```


## Combine indicators and create second subset

The combined indicator ranges from 0 to 2. A value of 1 can arise from either one of the two conditions.

```{r}
#| label: workshop-29
# ?ds.make  # interactive help 

ds.make(toAssign = "BMI.25.plus+GLUC.6.less",
        newobj = "BMI.25.plus_GLUC.6.less")

# If BMI >= 25 and glucose < 6, then BMI.25.plus_GLUC.6.less=2
# If BMI >= 25 and glucose >= 6, then BMI.25.plus_GLUC.6.less=1
# If BMI < 25 and glucose < 6, then BMI.25.plus_GLUC.6.less=1
# If BMI < 25 and glucose >= 6, then BMI.25.plus_GLUC.6.less=0

ds.table(rvar= "BMI.25.plus_GLUC.6.less",
         datasources = conns)

ds.dataFrame(x=c("D", "BMI.25.plus_GLUC.6.less"), newobj = "D2")

ds.colnames("D2")

ds.dataFrameSubset(df.name = "D2",
  V1.name = "D2$BMI.25.plus_GLUC.6.less",
  V2.name = "2",
  Boolean.operator = "==",
  newobj = "subset2")

ds.dim("subset2")
```

```{r}
           newobj = "workshop.obj")
model1
```



## Predict fitted values

```{r}

ds.length("workshop.prediction.obj$fit", datasources=conns)
ds.length("D$LAB_HDL", datasources=conns)
```


## Prepare complete-case variables

```{r}
#| label: workshop-39

ds.completeCases('vars', newobj='vars.complete')
ds.dim('vars.complete')
```


## Plot observations and fitted lines

This reproduces the original plotting commands. Check disclosure rules before requesting or publishing returned coordinates.

```{r}
#| label: workshop-40
df1 <- ds.scatterPlot('D$PM_BMI_CONTINUOUS', "D$LAB_HDL", return.coords = TRUE)
df2 <- ds.scatterPlot('vars.complete$PM_BMI_CONTINUOUS', "workshop.prediction.obj$fit",

# then in native R
par(mfrow=c(2,2))
plot(as.data.frame(df1[[1]][[1]])$x,
     as.data.frame(df1[[1]][[1]])$y, xlab='Body Mass Index', ylab='HDL Cholesterol', main='Study 1')
lines(as.data.frame(df2[[1]][[1]])$x,as.data.frame(df2[[1]][[1]])$y, col='red')
plot(as.data.frame(df1[[1]][[2]])$x,as.data.frame(df1[[1]][[2]])$y,

lines(as.data.frame(df2[[1]][[2]])$x,as.data.frame(df2[[1]][[2]])$y, col='red')
```


# 10. Model diagnostics


## Residual diagnostics

These are the original pooled-model residual calculations. Confirm model assumptions and coefficient extraction against the installed package version.

```{r}
#| label: workshop-41
glmslma <- ds.glmSLMA(formula = "vars.complete$LAB_HDL~vars.complete$PM_BMI_CONTINUOUS", family="gaussian", newobj = "workshop.obj")

ds.make(toAssign=paste0("(",glmslma$SLMA.pooled.ests.matrix[1,1],")+(", glmslma$SLMA.pooled.ests.matrix[2,1],"*vars.complete$PM_BMI_CONTINUOUS)"), 
        newobj = "predicted.values")

ds.make(toAssign = "vars.complete$LAB_HDL - predicted.values", 
        newobj = "residuals")

# and you can use those to run regression plot diagnostics  
ds.scatterPlot('predicted.values', "residuals")
ds.histogram("residuals")
```


# 11. Logistic regression and meta-analysis


## Diabetes frequencies

```{r}
#| label: workshop-42
ds.table("D$DIS_DIAB")
```


## Inspect diabetes class

```{r}
#| label: workshop-43
ds.class("D$DIS_DIAB")
```


## Logistic regression by study

```{r}
#| label: workshop-44
glmSLMA_mod2<-ds.glmSLMA(formula="D$DIS_DIAB~D$PM_BMI_CONTINUOUS", family='binomial')
glmSLMA_mod2
```


## Extract effect estimates and standard errors

```{r}
#| label: workshop-45
estimates <- c(glmSLMA_mod2$betamatrix.valid[2,])
se <- c(glmSLMA_mod2$sematrix.valid[2,])
```


## Random-effects meta-analysis

```{r}
#| label: workshop-46
res <- rma(estimates, sei=se)
```


## Basic forest plot

```{r}
#| label: workshop-47
forest(res, atransf=exp)
```


## Annotated forest plot

The original plot assumes two studies and fixed annotation positions; adjust if the server results differ.

```{r}
#| label: workshop-48
study_names <- c("France", "Spain")
weights <-  c(paste0(formatC(weights(res), format="f", digits=1, width=4), "%"))

forest(res, atransf=exp,
       xlab="Crude Odds Ratio", refline=log(1), xlim=c(-0.25,0.5), 
       at=log(c(0.95, 1, 1.1, 1.2, 1.3)),
       slab=cbind(paste0(study_names, " (", paste0(weights, ")"))), 
       mlab="RE model")
text(0.5, 4.5, pos=2, "Odds Ratio [95% CI]")
text(-0.25, 4.5, pos=4, "Study (weight)")
```


## Multivariable pooled logistic regression

```{r}
#| label: workshop-49
glm_mod1<-ds.glm(formula="D$DIS_DIAB~D$PM_BMI_CONTINUOUS+D$LAB_HDL*D$GENDER", family='binomial')
```


## Multivariable study-level logistic regression

```{r}
#| label: workshop-50
glmSLMA_mod2<-ds.glmSLMA(formula="D$DIS_DIAB~D$PM_BMI_CONTINUOUS+D$LAB_HDL*D$GENDER", family='binomial')
```


## Compare model coefficients

```{r}
#| label: workshop-51
glm_mod1$coefficients
glmSLMA_mod2$SLMA.pooled.ests.matrix
```
